experiments.scope: The sha256-r47-prefix-v1 target with 52-byte messages P || x (P = 20 zero bytes, x the 32-byte chain value, one block), collision of the low 18 bits of the complete digest. Each trial runs ONE attempt of the shipped 256-lane search on the walk g = f (plan(18): distinguished points with the low 2 bits zero, 8 batches of 256 lanes, cut rule, table, recovery on the rolled two-lane program) from a word derived from the trial seed, with no amplification, and returns the two 52-byte messages M(x) and M(y) when the attempt found a pair, two nulls otherwise. The program is the unrolled 256-lane program with the 238 high input planes zero. The same program also runs the same attempt on an ideal function of the same width (keyed blake2b) and one family-law run with a fresh random 20-byte prefix at n = 12; these are reported as untrusted observations only.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages are distinct and their complete 47-step digests agree in the low 18 bits (digest bytes 29, 30 and 31, the low 2 bits of byte 29). This is exact: the program recovers a merge of two trails of the walk g = f at width 18, and f is the digest minus the IV word by word, which keeps the low 18 bits bijective. The number of trials that return a pair is the number of single attempts that succeeded; it is reported as a program check, with the ideal-function control as an untrusted observation, and no probability, interval or sampling inference is drawn from it. Observations (untrusted, the program's own): target_ok, ideal_ok, batches, halts, t1_steps. Not shown: any width-256 cost or success probability.

experiments.scope: The sha256-r47-prefix-v1 target with 52-byte messages P || x (P = 20 zero bytes) at full width 256. Each trial evaluates 512 points x with the shipped program (source by trial index mod 3: uniform inputs from the seed, counter inputs r + i, iterates of g from 256 seed-derived starts), recovers the digests from the stored planes by adding the IV word by word, and returns two distinct points whose complete digests agree in the low 18 bits when the set contains such a pair, two nulls otherwise. Untrusted observations: the numbers of equal pairs in seven 18-bit projections of the digest.
experiments.hypothesis: For every returned pair the two messages M(x) and M(y) are distinct and their complete 47-step digests agree in the low 18 bits (digest bytes 29, 30 and 31, the low 2 bits of byte 29). This is exact: it checks the program, the IV addition and the message construction at full width. The number of returned pairs and the projection counts are reported as program checks, not as estimates, and no inference is drawn from them. Observations (untrusted): source, dup_w0, dup_w3, dup_w7, dup_xor8, dup_sum8, dup_p01, dup_p23. Not shown: collision structure at 2^128 evaluations.
